title: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
summary: The Supreme Court held that Parliament's power to amend the Constitution does not include the power to destroy its basic structure.
why_relevant: Foundational authority on constitutional limits and the basic-structure doctrine.

title: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
summary: Expanded Article 21 so that any procedure affecting life or personal liberty must be fair, just and reasonable.
why_relevant: Often cited for fairness of state action affecting liberty and travel.

title: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan
summary: Laid down binding workplace guidelines against sexual harassment pending legislation; later reflected in the POSH Act.
why_relevant: Key authority for workplace harassment and employer duties.

title: Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation
summary: Recognised livelihood as part of the right to life and required fair procedure before eviction of pavement dwellers.
why_relevant: Relevant to housing, eviction, and livelihood protections.

title: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
summary: Landmark ruling on reservations for Other Backward Classes, including the 50% ceiling and creamy-layer principle.
why_relevant: Core authority on public employment reservation policy.

title: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
summary: Held that privacy is a fundamental right under the Constitution.
why_relevant: Foundational for privacy, data protection, and surveillance questions.

title: National Legal Services Authority v. Union of India
summary: Recognised transgender persons as a third gender and affirmed equality and dignity protections.
why_relevant: Authority on gender identity and non-discrimination.

title: Common Cause v. Union of India
summary: Recognised passive euthanasia and living wills within Article 21 dignity framework.
why_relevant: Relevant to end-of-life medical decision-making and dignity.

title: Shayara Bano v. Union of India
summary: Struck down instant triple talaq as unconstitutional.
why_relevant: Key family-law authority on unilateral instantaneous divorce practice.

title: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum Gas Leak)
summary: Developed absolute liability for hazardous industries causing harm.
why_relevant: Foundational for industrial accidents and environmental harm claims.

title: Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh
summary: Mandatory registration of FIR for cognizable offences, with limited preliminary inquiry exceptions.
why_relevant: Core authority when police refuse to register an FIR.

title: Aruna Ramchandra Shanbaug v. Union of India
summary: Allowed passive euthanasia in limited circumstances under court supervision; later refined in Common Cause.
why_relevant: Earlier authority on withdrawal of life support.
